Article:
A new beginning this year for me. After 5 years at Agoda it is time for me to move on to new challenges.
I am going to do something I haven't done for a while: writing a resume. It needs to reflect my skills and experience without showing off. Or maybe a little bit, huh?
I'm going to take this opportunity to create it using good CSS3 and HTML5 practices. The first thing I have in mind is to limit the DOM depth. Resumes have simple structures, so we shouldn't need a long list of nested DIVs. It will render fast on the screen.
Second is to choosing a monospaced font so we can keep control of the format when printing. Let's throw in some font awesome to have a nice touch on the contact details.
Next, and not the least, content. Look isn't everything. There are many ways you can write a resume. One of them is NOT to write more than 2 pages. I have reviewed a lot of resumes in my Hiring Manager role, and boy have I seen 15+ pages of company descriptions, their products, sometimes their clients. All of that without the actual role and responsibilities the candidate had.
So I had to get some up-to-date documentation. I read a few advises and recommended ways to write a resume here and there. There is no shortcut, you need to spend the time to write it, proof-edit it yourself, give it to your family or friends to review. Several times.
You can see the current version here.

Grand opening of sawan.io.
This website is about my personal training on various web-technologies: TypeScript, webpack, ReactJS, Secure HTTP headers... It includes a simple (and a bit naive) crypto-currency analyser: it can suggest you to sell or buy. Use at your own risk, it is amateur predictions, you have been warned.
There will be also an application to track health metrics (weight, % body fat, vascular fat ratio...). Or maybe not, this might be my next project.
This project is open-sourced on Github. Enjoy and have fun.

So I have tried to bring some better support to the website in order editing/adding content. Here is what is new and so far well working:
  • Can see the last 4 blog posts on homepage (need to change to 3), content limited to 1000 characters (issue with --sorting-- fixed )
  • Can go to the full article
  • Can go to editable mode:
    • Can edit the content with real-time preview
    • Can save if you have the right permission
One condition to allow saving was to specify via environment variable the Google UserId that has the permission to save. You can see in this code the poor implementation. This is an initial stage so that I can post more regular update on the page (the MVP basically). So the next step is to implement a proper authentication via middle-ware.
Then I need to improve the WYSIWYG editor to be much more friendly, if I want to post richer content. The final intention of the blog is to post useful tutorials on what I have learned. And there are a lot of topics I need to share (like Certbot and Let's Encrypt for HTTPS support using open certificate authority, how to build a multi-stage docker image to create reproducible, stable development and build system, and more...).

Article:
This is something I have gathered through my few years as manager. More will be added or edited (or removed) as I capture/remember them.
  • Consistency is key
  • Feedback
    • Feedback is a powerful tool. Share feedback often, but not unnecessarily
    • Make sure you share positive feedback regularly, so when you have to deliver a negative one, the "average" is balanced
    • Always bring facts and/or data when delivering any feedback. Otherwise you will lose credibility
  • Your team
    • Your team needs a common goal they are attracted to / interested in:
      • One way to do it is to motivate them via meaningful KPI(s)
      • Give your team an idea of what a perfect world (relative to the team/company objectives) would be. Better, have them define what it would be. Then create a road-map towards it and ensure time is allocated to any elements of this road-map that are aligned with team/company objectives. Make sure some time is allocated to lower priority elements but that will contribute to the team happiness/motivation
    • Identify your team members individual personalities:
      • Starters vs Finishers
      • Introvert vs Extrovert
      • Skill level (relevant to the team purpose). Not to confuse with seniority.
      • Pro-active vs passive
      • Growth oriented vs complescent
      • Leader vs Follower
    • One on one
      • Do 1-on-1 regularly, in a very constructive manner
      • Start with the outcome/agreement status from previous 1-on-1
      • Share any new feedback, accompanied with the relevant fact or data
      • Ask for feedback. If the person isn't comfortable giving feedback, ask for a specific question
      • End with a commitment, goal or objective to reach, with a date it will be reached or reviewed. The commitment can be for either or both of you
    • Identify low performer. Inform the low performer (via facts and data) what he/she is not doing well enough.
      • That person might have not realized he/she wasn't performing and could transform to a good or even high performer
      • It will show the rest of the team you care about low performer that might be slowing their success down
      • No man/woman left behind
    • Similarly, identify high performer and give them challenges according to their aspirations: technical expertise or leadership role
    • Communicate regularly the company results to show they belong to a big thing, not just an silo
    • Have lunch with your team. Organize occasional outing
  • Working with data
    • Identify very early what kind of data will bring to your project/team/task a measure of success or failure
    • Try to automate as much as possible the collecting of data
    • You can interest your subordinate(s) to collect the data or create an automated tool as part of their learning/growth
    • Start a road-map. Now!
    • Share your road-map early with all stakeholders. It will help:
      • Confirming the requirements/scope
      • Explaining people or resource shortage
      • Providing a constructive support for project updates
      • Providing a form of burn-down / completion status report

If you're like me and want a minimal raspbian running on your pi but still with the desktop GUI, you have 2 alternatives:
  • Install the 'lite' version (~360MB) and do these minimal install steps:
    Edit '/etc/wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.conf'
    and add at the bottom
    network={
      ssid="YOUR_SSID"
      psk="YOUR_PASSWORD"
    }
    sudo apt update && sudo apt -y upgrade
    sudo reboot
    After reboot continue with
    sudo apt clean && sudo apt -y autoremove
    sudo apt install -y raspberrypi-ui-mods rpi-chromium-mods
    sudo reboot
  • Install the 'desktop' version (~1.2GB) and remove extra stuff:
    sudo apt purge -y scratch2 minecraft-pi wolfram-engine sonic-pi dillo libreoffice* squeak* geany
    sudo reboot
    After reboot continue with
    sudo apt clean && sudo apt -y autoremove
